note: Independent source rejudgment of RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1.2, including the full SPD-entry description: "One to N selector sets that correspond to the "condition" for applying a particular IPsec action." parseSPDPolicy constructs one set of local/remote prefixes, protocol and ports. N=1 meets this structural item; this does not establish multi-selector negotiation or the separately allocated users-MUST-NOT rule. Both tagged tests were read with holdsSelector: HoldsOneSelectorSet parses an operator tree and asserts exact local/remote prefixes, protocol 17, local port 53 and remote ANY; CannotCarryASecondSelectorSet counts four scalar prefix/port fields and rejects selector-bearing collections. Its reflection guard does not exhaust hypothetical recursively nested future models. The single-positive annotation is justified by this representation's fixed one-set cardinality, not by absence of all configuration error paths. The current exhaustive-ignore directives only document deliberately narrow reflection switches; assertions and selector construction remain substantive. Verdict enforced. No tests or discrimination replay executed by this auditor.
